design.hiddenRule: A step is good iff the running-total result stated in its natural-language sentence equals the hidden true arithmetic running total. Good and bad variants use the same template, delta and operation; only the stated result differs by 1-3. No label appears in the text.
design.groundTruth: step.good (per step) and finalCorrect (last step) / trajectory
design.split: first 50 generated trajectories train, last 50 holdout; labels are not used to build features

untrained.finalStepAucNote: AUC of the last-step heuristic score against trajectory finalCorrect. All general heuristic scores tie, so this is 0.5.

oracleStepLabels.purpose: Upper-bound check: even with perfect per-step labels, the trainer exposes no model for holdout inference.

decision.rule: add-opt-in iff holdout AUC >= 0.7 AND (trained AUC - untrained AUC) >= 0.05
reasons: holdout scores are identical before and after trainer.train(): no trained state is consumed by the scorer
PRMTrainer exposes no inference method (prototype: computeLoss, train, validate, cosineLR, linearDecayLR, shuffleIndices); train() only returns loss history
weak-supervision labels collapse to 2 distinct values (trajectory outcome, not per-step quality)

limitations: Synthetic arithmetic trajectories only; no LLM-generated reasoning and no Monte Carlo rollouts/real verifier.
scorePathHeuristic('general') is length/structure-based and ignores numeric correctness; the math heuristic also cannot verify the hidden arithmetic rule.

PRMTrainer.train() fits scalar predictions initialized as label*0.5+0.25, indexed by training sample; it returns only { history, finalLoss } and exposes no predict/infer method. There is no learned weight vector to apply to holdout.
ProcessRewardModel cannot load trainer state; re-scoring the holdout set after training is byte-identical.
With tied heuristic scores, labelSteps weak supervision produces only two label values driven by trajectory outcome; it provides no per-step quality signal.
All heuristic scores tie at 0.65, so AUC is exactly 0.5 by the average-rank convention and precision/recall at a 0.5 threshold predict every step positive.
The oracle-label trainer run confirms the limitation is structural (no inference path), not merely a weak-label issue.
Registered scorers and the score cache exist in ProcessRewardModel but are not used by scorePathHeuristic; they do not constitute a trainable PRM.
